Decompose a treatment effect into mediated and calibrated contrasts

Source: R/calibrated-contrasts.R
calibrated_contrasts.Rd

Given estimates of the risk of an outcome under treatment, under placebo, and under a calibrated intervention (as returned by tmle_alpha() and calibrate_alpha()), computes the total treatment effect and its decomposition into a mediated contrast (treatment versus calibrated) and a calibrated contrast (calibrated versus placebo), with Wald confidence intervals based on the influence curves.

Usage

calibrated_contrasts(
  treatment_fit,
  placebo_fit,
  calibrated_fit,
  target = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

treatment_fit, placebo_fit

Fits for the treatment and placebo arms, as returned by tmle_alpha().

calibrated_fit

Fit for the calibrated intervention, as returned by calibrate_alpha().

target

Optional string. If calibrated_fit contains estimates for several targets, the name of the one to use.

conf_level

Number between 0 and 1. Confidence level of the intervals.

Value

A data.table with one row per contrast (total, mediated and calibrated) and columns target (NA if target is NULL), contrast, estimate, se, lower and upper. The attributes decomposition_error and eic_decomposition_error give how far the estimates and influence curves are from satisfying total = mediated + calibrated, which should be zero up to numerical error.

Examples

set.seed(1405)
treatment_fit <- list(estimate = c(tmle_est = 0.7), eic = rnorm(200, sd = 0.1))
placebo_fit <- list(estimate = c(tmle_est = 0.3), eic = rnorm(200, sd = 0.1))
calibrated_fit <- list(estimate = c(target_est = 0.5), eic = rnorm(200, sd = 0.1))

calibrated_contrasts(treatment_fit, placebo_fit, calibrated_fit)
#>    target   contrast estimate         se     lower     upper
#>    <char>     <char>    <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>
#> 1:   <NA>      total      0.4 0.01028048 0.3798506 0.4201494
#> 2:   <NA>   mediated      0.2 0.01050568 0.1794092 0.2205908
#> 3:   <NA> calibrated      0.2 0.01028145 0.1798487 0.2201513
